knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_isoniazid_6h"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18080937> (open access;
  the supplement contains the authors' Stan / R code and Tables S1-S8)

Li et al. (2026) fitted three **independent** regimen-specific Bayesian
population PK models for oral isoniazid in adults receiving tuberculosis
preventive therapy:

| Regimen | Isoniazid | Rifamycin | Model |
|---------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| 6H | 300 mg once daily, 6 months | none | `Li_2026_isoniazid_6h` |
| 3HR | 300 mg once daily, 3 months | rifampicin 450 mg (<50 kg) / 600 mg (>=50 kg) daily | `Li_2026_isoniazid_3hr` |
| 3H2P2 | 300 mg twice weekly, 3 months | rifapentine 500 mg (<50 kg) / 600 mg (>=50 kg) twice weekly | `Li_2026_isoniazid_3h2p2` |

Each model is a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and
elimination. Apparent oral clearance depends on NAT2 acetylator phenotype
(intermediate acetylator reference) and on body weight; apparent volume
depends on body weight. The weight terms are normalised to each regimen's own
median weight, because the authors' code centres weight within each
regimen's dataset. The rifamycin interaction is not a covariate: it is
carried entirely by the regimen-specific typical values of CL/F, V/F and ka.

```{r descriptions, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (nm in c("Li_2026_isoniazid_6h", "Li_2026_isoniazid_3hr", "Li_2026_isoniazid_3h2p2")) {
  cat("* `", nm, "`: ", rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm))$description, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Population

The 173 participants with latent tuberculosis infection were recruited in
Sichuan Province, China, between July 2024 and June 2025 in a prospective
observational study (Methods 2.1). Plasma was sampled after two weeks of
treatment, predose and 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 h after a dose. Concentrations below
the limit of quantification (25-31% of samples) were handled with the M3
likelihood. Baseline characteristics (Table 1):

| | 6H | 3HR | 3H2P2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subjects (observations) | 62 (372) | 53 (318) | 58 (348) |
| Age, years, median (IQR) | 38 (32.3-45.3) | 39 (33.3-45.7) | 38 (32.4-46.5) |
| Male, n (%) | 31 (50.0) | 25 (47.2) | 25 (43.1) |
| Weight, kg, median (IQR) | 66.4 (59.0-72.0) | 61.7 (57.8-69.1) | 58.9 (53.9-69.3) |
| NAT2 slow / intermediate / fast, n | 20 / 18 / 24 | 19 / 21 / 13 | 16 / 23 / 19 |
| BLQ observations, % | 25.3 | 29.9 | 30.5 |

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Li_2026_isoniazid_6h")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | 6H | 3HR | 3H2P2 | Source location |
|----------------------|----|-----|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka, 1/h) | log(2.88) | log(2.71) | log(2.88) | Table 2; Results 3.2.1-3.2.3 |
| `lcl` (CL/F, L/h) | log(21.83) | log(26.32) | log(25.98) | Table 2; Results 3.2.1-3.2.3 |
| `lvc` (V/F, L) | log(51.03) | log(45.91) | log(50.24) | Table 2; Results 3.2.1-3.2.3 |
| Reference weight (kg) | 66.4 | 61.7 | 58.9 | Table 1 regimen medians; Supplementary Code `prepare_regimen_data()` |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.728 | 0.728 | 0.728 | Table 2 / Results 3.2 ('across regimens') |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.999 | 0.999 | 0.999 | Table 2 / Results 3.2 |
| `e_nat2_slow_cl` | log(0.646) | log(0.646) | log(0.646) | Table 3; Results 3.2.4 (slow vs intermediate, -35.4%) |
| `e_nat2_rapid_cl` | log(1.484) | log(1.484) | log(1.484) | Table 3; Results 3.2.4 (fast vs intermediate, +48.4%) |
| `etalcl` | 0.05157 | 0.05157 | 0.05157 | Table 2: 23.00 %CV; omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) |
| `etalvc` | 0.006348 | 0.006348 | 0.006348 | Table 2: 7.98 %CV; omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) |
| `expSd` | 0.895 | 0.895 | 0.895 | Table 2: proportional error, log-scale SD |
| `cl = exp(lcl + beta_nat2 + etalcl) * (WT/WTref)^e_wt_cl` | | | | Supplementary Code, Stan `model` block |
| `vc = exp(lvc + etalvc) * (WT/WTref)^e_wt_vc` | | | | Supplementary Code, Stan `model` block |
| One-compartment first-order absorption | | | | Results 3.2; Stan function `oral_one_cpt()` |
| `Cc ~ lnorm(expSd)` | | | | Stan likelihood `log(conc) ~ normal(log(Cpred), sigma)`; Table S1 |

# Replicate Table 4: typical-value exposure by regimen and NAT2

Table 4 reports simulated AUC0-24 and Cmax after one isoniazid dose for each
regimen and NAT2 phenotype, with body weight held at its typical value and no
between-subject variability (the exposure-simulation function in the
Supplementary Code draws posterior parameters but no etas). The authors
also multiplied the 300 mg dose by a "relative bioavailability factor" of
1.0 (6H), 0.8 (3HR) and 0.85 (3H2P2) that is **not** part of the fitted
model (Table S3: "Relative F applied as effective dose = Dose * F_rel, not by
changing the fitted Stan model"). The same effective doses are used here so
that the comparison is like for like; see Assumptions and deviations.

```{r table4-sim}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~model, ~wt_ref, ~frel, ~ii,
  "6H", "Li_2026_isoniazid_6h", 66.4, 1.00, 24,
  "3HR", "Li_2026_isoniazid_3hr", 61.7, 0.80, 24,
  "3H2P2", "Li_2026_isoniazid_3h2p2", 58.9, 0.85, 84
)
nat2_levels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~nat2, ~NAT2_SLOW, ~NAT2_RAPID,
  "Slow", 1, 0,
  "Intermediate", 0, 0,
  "Fast", 0, 1
)
obs_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)

typ_one <- function(reg) {
  r <- regimens[regimens$regimen == reg, ]
  ev <- tidyr::crossing(nat2_levels, time = obs_grid) |>
    mutate(id = match(nat2, nat2_levels$nat2), evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  doses <- nat2_levels |>
    mutate(id = seq_len(n()), time = 0, evid = 1, amt = 300 * r$frel, cmt = "depot")
  ev <- bind_rows(doses, ev) |>
    mutate(WT = r$wt_ref) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  mod <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(r$model)())
  # Typical-value solve of three subjects with the random effects removed:
  # rxode2 notes this ("multi-subject simulation without ... 'omega'"),
  # which is exactly what is intended here, so only that condition is muffled.
  sim <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = c("nat2"), returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("multi-subject simulation without", conditionMessage(w))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    },
    message = function(m) {
      if (grepl("omega/sigma items treated as zero", conditionMessage(m))) {
        invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
      }
    }
  )
  sim$regimen <- reg
  list(sim = sim, doses = doses |> mutate(regimen = reg))
}
typ <- lapply(regimens$regimen, typ_one)
sim_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(typ, `[[`, "sim"))
dose_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(typ, `[[`, "doses"))
```

```{r table4-pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(regimen, nat2, id, time, Cc)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(regimen, nat2, id) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(regimen, nat2, id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(regimen, nat2, id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + nat2 + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_typ |> select(regimen, nat2, id, time, amt),
  amt ~ time | regimen + nat2 + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_t4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~nat2, ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "6H", "Slow", 20.85, 4.52,
  "6H", "Intermediate", 13.29, 4.03,
  "6H", "Fast", 8.81, 3.64,
  "3HR", "Slow", 14.10, 3.83,
  "3HR", "Intermediate", 8.99, 3.39,
  "3HR", "Fast", 6.20, 3.13,
  "3H2P2", "Slow", 16.04, 4.13,
  "3H2P2", "Intermediate", 9.85, 3.50,
  "3H2P2", "Fast", 6.76, 3.25
)

cmp_t4 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_typ,
  reference = published_t4,
  by = c("regimen", "nat2"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_t4,
  caption = "Typical-value AUC0-24 and Cmax vs. Table 4 medians (Li 2026). * differs from the reference by >20%."
)
```

```{r table4-check}
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_typ$result) |>
  select(regimen, nat2, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(published_t4, by = c("regimen", "nat2"), suffix = c("_sim", "_pub")) |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auclast_sim - auclast_pub) / auclast_pub,
    cmax_pct = 100 * (cmax_sim - cmax_pub) / cmax_pub
  )
# Deterministic typical-value solves against posterior-median summaries:
# the difference comes from posterior parameter uncertainty in Table 4 and
# from Table 4's rounded NAT2 multipliers (0.65 / 1.5, Table S3), so a
# 10% band is ample while a mis-transcribed CL/F or dose would break it.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_wide$auc_pct) < 10),
  all(abs(nca_wide$cmax_pct) < 10)
)
```

All nine AUC0-24 values reproduce Table 4 within about 5.5% and Cmax within
about 7.5%. The residual differences come from the summary statistic (Table 4
reports the median over posterior draws, which include parameter
uncertainty; the packaged model is the posterior median) and from Table 4's
rounded NAT2 multipliers of 0.65 and 1.5 (Table S3) against the reported
effect ratios 0.646 and 1.484 used in the models.

# Replicate Figure 4: visual predictive check by regimen

Figure 4 shows VPCs over the 0-8 h sampling window after two weeks of
treatment. The virtual cohort below draws 200 participants per regimen with
log-normal body weight matched to each regimen's median and IQR (Table 1) and
NAT2 phenotype sampled at each regimen's observed proportions. Doses are the
nominal 300 mg (no relative-bioavailability factor), once daily for 6H and
3HR and every 84 h for 3H2P2, with sampling after the last dose of week 2.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260602)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260602)
n_per_arm <- 200

cohort_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~wt_med, ~wt_q1, ~wt_q3, ~p_slow, ~p_int, ~p_fast, ~n_doses,
  "6H", 66.4, 59.0, 72.0, 20 / 62, 18 / 62, 24 / 62, 14,
  "3HR", 61.7, 57.8, 69.1, 19 / 53, 21 / 53, 13 / 53, 14,
  "3H2P2", 58.9, 53.9, 69.3, 16 / 58, 23 / 58, 19 / 58, 4
)

make_cohort <- function(reg, id_offset) {
  s <- cohort_spec[cohort_spec$regimen == reg, ]
  r <- regimens[regimens$regimen == reg, ]
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    WT = exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, log(s$wt_med), log(s$wt_q3 / s$wt_q1) / (2 * qnorm(0.75)))),
    nat2 = sample(c("Slow", "Intermediate", "Fast"), n_per_arm,
      replace = TRUE, prob = c(s$p_slow, s$p_int, s$p_fast)
    )
  ) |>
    left_join(nat2_levels, by = "nat2")
  last_dose <- (s$n_doses - 1) * r$ii
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose_no = seq_len(s$n_doses)) |>
    mutate(time = (dose_no - 1) * r$ii, evid = 1, amt = 300, cmt = "depot") |>
    select(-dose_no)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(tad = c(seq(0, 8, by = 0.25))) |>
    mutate(time = last_dose + tad, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central") |>
    select(-tad)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(regimen = reg, tlast = last_dose) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
offsets <- c("6H" = 0L, "3HR" = 1000L, "3H2P2" = 2000L)
cohorts <- lapply(regimens$regimen, function(reg) make_cohort(reg, offsets[[reg]]))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unlist(lapply(cohorts, function(d) unique(d$id)))))
```

```{r vpc-sim}
sim_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  mod <- readModelDb(regimens$model[i])()
  ev <- cohorts[[i]]
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = c("regimen", "nat2", "WT", "tlast"), returnType = "data.frame")
  out
})) |>
  mutate(tad = time - tlast, regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  group_by(regimen, tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Isoniazid concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated 5th / 50th / 95th percentiles (with residual error)",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 4A of Li 2026 (no observed data overlaid)."
  )
```

The simulated individual Cmax is about 4 mg/L (geometric mean, steady-state
NCA below) at a median Tmax of 0.75 h, and concentrations fall several-fold
over the 8 h window, bracketing the observed median of 1.5-1.7 mg/L over all
sampling times (Table 1). The very wide
5th-95th percentile band reflects the log-scale residual SD of 0.895, which
the authors estimated jointly with 25-31% left-censored data.

# Individual clearance by regimen and NAT2 (Table S2)

Table S2 reports the median post-hoc CL/F by regimen and NAT2 phenotype,
which reflect the observed weight distribution and between-subject
variability. The simulated individual clearances from the same virtual cohort
are compared below.

```{r table-s2}
published_s2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~nat2, ~cl_pub,
  "6H", "Slow", 13.6, "6H", "Intermediate", 21.1, "6H", "Fast", 32.1,
  "3HR", "Slow", 16.2, "3HR", "Intermediate", 25.3, "3HR", "Fast", 38.4,
  "3H2P2", "Slow", 15.9, "3H2P2", "Intermediate", 24.9, "3H2P2", "Fast", 37.7
)
cl_cmp <- sim_vpc |>
  distinct(regimen, id, nat2, cl) |>
  group_by(regimen, nat2) |>
  summarise(n = n(), cl_sim = median(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  left_join(published_s2, by = c("regimen", "nat2")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cl_sim - cl_pub) / cl_pub)

cl_cmp |>
  mutate(cl_sim = signif(cl_sim, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "NAT2" = nat2, "Simulated n" = n,
    "Simulated median CL/F (L/h)" = cl_sim, "Table S2 median CL/F (L/h)" = cl_pub,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median individual CL/F, simulated cohort vs. Table S2 post-hoc estimates.")

# Each stratum median carries Monte Carlo noise from ~40-90 virtual
# subjects with 23% CV IIV, so assert on the centre and a robust quantile.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cl_cmp$pct_diff)) < 8,
  quantile(abs(cl_cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 15
)
```

# Steady-state NCA of the virtual cohort

```{r pknca-vpc}
# The observation grid starts at tad = 0 (the trough at the last dose), so
# every subject already has a time-zero record.
ss_nca <- sim_vpc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(regimen, id, tad, Cc) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen))
stopifnot(all(tapply(ss_nca$tad, ss_nca$id, min) == 0))
ss_dose <- ss_nca |> distinct(regimen, id) |> mutate(tad = 0, amt = 300)
ss_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(ss_nca, Cc ~ tad | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ss_dose, amt ~ tad | regimen + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
)
ss_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(ss_obj)
summary(ss_res)
```

The paper reports no observed NCA, so this table is descriptive. The 0-8 h
window matches the study sampling schedule.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Three independent models, shared reporting.** The authors fitted each
  regimen independently (Supplementary Code: "No CL/F, V/F, Ka, NAT2 effect,
  body-weight effect, IIV, or residual-error parameter was shared across
  regimens"), but the paper prints regimen-specific values only for CL/F,
  V/F and ka. The weight exponents, NAT2 effects, IIV and residual error are
  reported once, as subject-number-weighted summaries across the three fits
  (Methods 2.3; Table 2 "Allometric exponents", "Residual variability",
  "Inter-individual variability"; Table 3). Those summary values are used in
  all three models, since the regimen-specific estimates are not published.
- **Relative-bioavailability factors are not in the models.** Table 4 and
  Table S2 multiply the 300 mg dose by 0.8 (3HR) and 0.85 (3H2P2). Table S3
  states that this was applied in the exposure simulations only, not in the
  fitted model, so the packaged models have no bioavailability term. The
  Table 4 replication above applies the same factors to the dose to match
  the published simulation; the Figure 4 VPC and Table S2 comparison use the
  nominal 300 mg dose, as in the fitted model. Because the rifamycin effect
  is already carried by the higher regimen-specific CL/F, applying these
  factors on top double-counts part of the interaction; users simulating
  rifamycin regimens should decide deliberately whether to apply them.
- **Reference weight.** The Stan code centres weight as log(WT / median WT)
  within each regimen's dataset; the per-regimen medians from Table 1 (66.4,
  61.7 and 58.9 kg) are used as the reference weights. The Table 3
  "per 10 kg" effects (+11.3% on CL/F, +15.9% on V/F) are consistent with the
  Table 2 exponents at these reference weights.
- **NAT2 reference phenotype.** Table 3, Results 3.2.4, the abstract and
  Table S2 all express the NAT2 effect against the intermediate acetylator
  (slow 0.646, fast 1.484), and the Stan code sets intermediate as the
  reference level. Figure 1 is titled "Ratio vs Slow Acetylator" and plots
  identical ratios of about 1.2 (intermediate) and 1.45 (fast) for all three
  regimens; these do not agree with Table 3 (which implies 1.55 and 2.30
  against slow) or with the post-hoc clearances of Table S2. The Table 3
  values are used.
- **Ka has no IIV**, matching the Stan code (`KAn = exp(log_KA)`).
- **Residual error.** The Stan likelihood is `log(conc) ~ normal(log(Cpred),
  sigma)`, encoded as `lnorm(expSd)`. Concentrations below the LLOQ were
  handled by the M3 method; the assay LLOQ is not reported, so no BLQ VPC
  (Figure 4B) is reproduced.
- **Rifamycin PK models are not packaged.** The paper describes INH and
  rifampicin / rifapentine models as joint for 3HR and 3H2P2 (Methods 2.2)
  and shows rifamycin VPCs in Figure S1, but no rifampicin or rifapentine
  parameter estimates are reported anywhere in the paper or supplement, and
  the published code fits isoniazid alone. Only the isoniazid models are
  packaged.
- **Table S2 exposure columns.** Table S2's AUC0-24 values (e.g. 132 mg*h/L
  for 6H slow acetylators) are inconsistent with its own CL/F column
  (300 mg / 13.6 L/h = 22 mg*h/L) and with Table 4; only its CL/F column is
  used for validation.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight is log-normal with each regimen's median
  and IQR from Table 1; age and sex are not model covariates. The 3H2P2
  dosing interval is 84 h, the value used for that regimen in the authors'
  code (`tau_by_regimen`).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-16.
